skills.name: Expansion and consolidation of German rule

note.text: After the coastal claim, Germany extended control inland through expeditions, treaties, military campaigns, stations and alliances. Consolidation involved making authority effective, collecting revenue and securing labour and routes. Existing African states and communities were not empty spaces waiting to be administered. Expansion was uneven and contested, and local intermediaries influenced its course. A map of a claimed colony should not be mistaken for proof that every locality was immediately under equally effective control.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: After the coastal claim, Germany extended control inland through expeditions, treaties, military campaigns, stations and alliances. Consolidation involved making authority effective, collecting revenue and securing labour and routes. Existing African states and communities were not empty spaces waiting to be administered. Expansion was uneven and contested, and local intermediaries influenced its course. A map of a claimed colony should not be mistaken for proof that every locality was immediately under equally effective control.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: An official station could support communication and administration, while soldiers and armed expeditions imposed demands. A ruler might negotiate in one period and oppose a later demand. Study the relationship between claimed territory, actual institutions and evidence of resistance rather than assuming that a flag instantaneously completed conquest.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the method and the place. Compare a colonial claim with evidence of stations, enforcement and local response. Describe coercion explicitly when force or threat shaped an agreement. Treat alliances as historical choices in changing conditions, not proof that one people had a fixed unchanging attitude.

key_words.meaning: armed movement intended to impose or extend authority
a local base supporting colonial authority
cooperation between actors for particular aims
extension of authority challenged by local action

Officials establish a post for communication and enforcement.
A local ruler cooperates with colonial agents against a rival.
